traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 85 Thymelaeaceae: trees or shrubs, rarely herbs; leaves opposite or alternate, mostly small; no stipules; flowers often in bracted heads, spikes or racemes, rarely alone, bisexual or of one sex, regular or slightly irregular; calyx a tube, sometimes petal-like, its lobes 4 or 5 (read as a hypanthium crowned by the lobes); petals scale-like or none; ovary superior; fruit staying shut (drupes and nuts in Daphne and kin), left unstated. Head-like clusters from 'terminal bracteate heads' (the OCR is broken there; inferred).
